title: A Crown for the Spire Anew
premise: Quentin Ashgrove has spent a decade guarding the sealed Thornfell gate, content to be forgotten by the kingdom that once branded them a deserter. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into their hands—a map showing the gate is not the only door, and the others are already opening—Quentin becomes the most hunted person in two realms. Forced to ally with Serah Vane, a royal inquisitor sent to silence them, Quentin must choose between destroying the map and using it to reach the spire where the old war's true cause still sleeps. In the end, Quentin seals the final gate from the inside at terrible cost, while Serah carries their story home—proof that belonging can be built, not granted.
about_author: Oscar Voss is a former cartographer who spent years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy rooted in borders, exile, and the quiet heroism of people history forgets.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Nothing
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A portrait of routine: tending the sealed gate, trading with smugglers who respect the rules of invisibility. A fevered stranger stumbles through a snowstorm clutching a leather tube. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace, shattered by the stranger's dying words—'the doors are singing.'

chapters.title: What the Dying Carry
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The stranger dies; the map reveals six gates across the Thornfells, five marked with fresh ink. Quentin burns nothing, decides nothing, but pockets the map—and hears, faintly, humming from the stone. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into dread as the past knocks.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Road
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. Sent from the capital to retrieve a stolen map and execute its holder, Serah tracks Quentin through smuggler country, noting how the mountains themselves seem to resist her. Emotional beat: duty sharpening into unease—her orders describe a thief, not a gatekeeper.

chapters.title: Two Shadows on One Pass
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Serah corners Quentin at a smuggler waystation; a third party—hooded, armed with old sigils—attacks them both. Fleeing together, they trade half-truths. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of necessity, each hiding what they know about the map.

chapters.title: The Second Door
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They reach a marked gate already cracked open, its ward-stones defaced. Inside: evidence someone from the capital authorized the opening. Serah realizes her superiors are complicit. Emotional beat: betrayal—the war isn't threatening to return; it's being invited back.

chapters.title: Ashgrove's Name
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Around a fire, Quentin's history surfaces: they didn't desert—they refused an order to open the first gate during the last crisis, and were erased for it. Serah must reconcile the traitor in her file with the keeper before her. Emotional beat: love stirring against duty, unspoken.

chapters.title: The Hunt Ascendant
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Royal hunters close in; the hooded faction strikes again, wounding Serah. Quentin chooses the forbidden route—through the smugglers' deep roads—to reach the sixth gate at the Spire Anew. Emotional beat: sacrifice accepted; invisibility abandoned forever.

chapters.title: Where the War Sleeps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Beneath the spire, they find the truth: the ancient war never ended—it was paused by a bargain, and the gates are its heartbeat. The hooded faction offers Quentin restoration, honor, everything owed. Emotional beat: temptation at its purest—belonging offered at exactly the wrong price.

chapters.title: A Crown for the Spire
chapters.summary: Serah's POV, climax. Serah arrives to arrest Quentin and instead turns her blade on the faction when they force the final gate. Quentin enters the closing mechanism alone, sealing it from within as the mountain groans shut. Emotional beat: love declared in the moment it must be surrendered.

chapters.title: The Keeper Remembered
chapters.summary: Serah's POV, resolution. Months later, Serah stands before the sealed spire, having testified against her superiors and rewritten Quentin's record. She leaves a crown of mountain flowers on the stone—and hears, very faintly, a knock answered by warmth, not war. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging; the gate holds, and so does she.
